about: The canonical item order, as data. `items` is deliberately shuffled; sorting it with items.order_items() must produce exactly `expected_order`. Each entry in `covers` names the tier of items.item_sort_key that the pair immediately around it exercises, so a failure says which tier moved.
covers: 1. content group: security, fixes, features, notes (t#c before t#g)
3. direction: reaches, unclear, does_not_reach, no local block (t#f before t#e)
4. effect: risk, none, benefit, no local block (t#g before t#f)
5. id ascending — the tiebreak that makes the order total (t#b before t#l)
an unrecognized tag groups under notes and nowhere else (t#h)
an unrecognized severity sorts after info within its group, never as one of the four (t#i)
a multi-tag item takes the highest-precedence group its tags name (t#j)

watch_hit is not a sort tier — two items identical on every tier sort by id whether or not one answers a watch item (t#m before t#n by id alone). Prominence is the highlight and the badge, never the order.
